title: feat(plugin-kanban): declare the four array/object-armed spec keys `object-kanban` already honours
body:
Fixes #8313

Slice 2a of objectui#8201, board package (the Q2 = B split). `object-kanban` / `view:kanban` now
declare `data`, `cardFields`, `grouping` and `conditionalFormatting` on the ONE shared `inputs`
list both tags spread, so the html tier stops reporting working metadata as `unknown-prop`.

## Per-key verdict

| key | declared arm | renderer honours it? | the sink, and WHICH QUESTION the member pin asks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `array` | yes | Read TWICE. As a GATE it suppresses the board's own query; as a VALUE, `rawData = external \|\| boundData \|\| schema.data \|\| fetchedData` selects it and `effectiveData` REBUILDS every member into a card. ⛔ No identity claim is true of it. The pin asks what is read INSIDE a member: `id` (or `_id`) as the card identity, the `groupBy` field's value as the lane, the title field, the `cardFields` cells. |
| `cardFields` | `array` | yes | `resolveKanbanCardFields(schema.cardFields, objectDef)`, exported and pure. The pin asks WHICH NAMES THE AUTHOR CHOSE — authored order, and NOT filtered against the object definition, which is the one behaviour separating the explicit list from the `highlightFields` fallback it overrides (that fallback IS filtered). WHICH CELLS THE CARD CARRIES is a second, narrower question and the pin shows the two answers differing. |
| `grouping` | `object` | yes, at exactly one position | `schema.grouping?.fields?.[0]?.field`, and only as the FALLBACK for `swimlaneField`. The pin asks which single nested position is read and under what precedence: the lanes appear keyed by `fields[0].field`; an explicit `swimlaneField` WINS; a second `fields` entry changes nothing. |
| `conditionalFormatting` | `array` | yes | The only one of the four `ObjectKanban.tsx` names NOWHERE (measured: 0 occurrences, control `cardFields` = 9). It rides the `{ ...schema }` spread into `effectiveSchema`, then `KanbanRenderer` forwards it to `KanbanImpl`'s `getCardStyles`. The pin asks which member dialects are evaluated and against what: native `{ field, operator, value }` and spec CEL `{ condition }`, per card, on that card's own record. |

No key was escalated. All four are measurements, not product rulings.

## Clause ② — what declaring them widens, and on what grounds

Declaring an input widens the authoring surface. The grounds are the ones objectui#8186 (`filter`)
and objectui#8223 (`sort`) cleared on: the SPEC already declares all four and the RENDERER already
honours all four, so this restores `declared = enforced` rather than publishing anything new.

Measured with a control on the same `safeParse` call, because "the spec declares it" is exactly the
assumption objectui#8172 falsified for `limit`: an unrecognised probe key draws `unrecognized_keys`
on that call while none of the four does. Read off the installed spec 17.3.0: `data` is
`z.array(z.unknown()).optional()`, `cardFields` is `z.array(z.string()).optional()`, `grouping` and
`conditionalFormatting` are both `z.unknown().optional()` — so for two of the four the contract
fixes the container kind only, and for the other two it constrains nothing at all. That is why the
read site is the whole of the member contract here.

⚠️ Three of the four are honoured only in PART, and a declaration that recommends a write the
renderer would drop is this gate's own failure mode one layer in. So each declared `description`
NAMES the position it is true about (`grouping` only at `fields[0].field` and only as the fallback;
`cardFields` as bare names, not entry objects; `data` as a fetch suppressor as well as a value), and
a row in the declaration pin asserts those sentences stay in the descriptions.

## The three-part obligation, paid per key in the same change

1. the `inputs` entry — all four, on the shared list;
2. the `UNPUBLISHED_EXEMPTIONS` entry DELETED — all four;
3. a `MEMBER_PINS` entry — all four. ⛔ Never a member-pin exemption.

`MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` stays **62**. Measured over the ledger: the member population grows
84 → 88 and the pin count 22 → 26, while `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` is byte-identical. Four new
array-armed keys at once could not be absorbed by headroom, because there is none — which is the
demonstration that ratchet's docblock claims, and a line recording it is added there.

**Both halves** of the shrink-only backlog ceiling move **8 → 4** (`toBeLessThanOrEqual` and `toBe`,
same `it()`).

## Which number I started from, and `quickAdd`

I started from **8**, re-derived on my own base rather than taken from the brief: `toBe(8)` and
`toBeLessThanOrEqual(8)` both present, all seven slice-1 keys present in the registration, and the
shared-list collapse in place (a grep for a slice-1 key returns 1, not 2 — the intended shape).

`object-kanban.quickAdd` is **still in that 8 and is NOT counted here**. Its carve-out (objectui#8285,
ruled a premature carve-out on objectui#8201 Q1 = A) had not landed on `main` when this branch was
cut and its exemption entry is untouched. It rides in its own change: it is a product ruling, not a
measurement, and this PR has no standing to write its reason. After this lands the backlog is 4 —
one `object-kanban` key (`quickAdd`) and three `object-calendar` keys — and the ceiling `it()` now
says so, including that "one key left" must not be read as "nearly done".

⚠️ Merge note: objectui#8285 and this PR both move the ceiling. Whichever lands second resolves a
one-line conflict and lowers the number again.

## Ablation — every new pin proved able to fail

Every leg: mutate, prove the mutation reached disk (marker counts before/after plus the matched
lines, and `git hash-object` differing from `git rev-parse HEAD:PATH`), run, then restore BY STATE
(`git diff HEAD` empty AND `git hash-object` equal again) — never by an exit code. All legs ran from
a committed implementation, with a restore trap on absolute paths.

**Declaration rows — BY NAME and PER REGISTRATION.** Deleting each `inputs` entry in turn reddens
two separate named rows per tag, e.g. for `grouping`:

```
× 'object-kanban' — the html tier accepts an authored `'grouping'`
× 'view:kanban'   — the html tier accepts an authored `'grouping'`
× 'object-kanban' — the registration declares `'grouping'` as `'object'`
× 'view:kanban'   — the registration declares `'grouping'` as `'object'`
× both tags publish ONE shared list, so a hand-copy cannot drift
× every declared description says what the renderer actually reads
× object-kanban publishes every top-level key its spec props schema declares   (parity gate)
× every member pin names a key that is still array/object-armed on a covered block   (parity gate)
```

Identical shape for `data`, `cardFields` and `conditionalFormatting`: 8 failed / 211 passed each.

**Member pins — mutate the READ SITE, not the pin.**

| mutation | red rows |
|---|---|
| `resolveKanbanCardFields` starts filtering the explicit list | the three `cardFields` rows, by name |
| `grouping?.fields?.[0]` → `[1]` | `fields[0].field` becomes the swimlane field; a SECOND `fields` entry is inert |
| the `{ ...schema }` spread stops carrying `conditionalFormatting` | both dialect rows + the "never NAMES this key" row |

**Ceiling, both halves, at the NEW number.** `toBe(4)` → `toBe(8)`: red, "the backlog shrank — lower
the ceiling above to match". Backlog grown to 5 (one input un-declared and its exemption re-added,
i.e. the exact move the ratchet exists to refuse): red, "the backlog list is shrink-only: expected 5
to be less than or equal to 4".

**Obligations ② and ③.** Re-adding a deleted exemption while its input is declared: red on `carries
no stale unpublished-key exemption`, naming it. Converting one `MEMBER_PINS` entry into a member-pin
exemption: red on `the member-pin exemption list only ratchets DOWN` (63 vs 62) AND on `the ceiling
correction admits exactly the four keys objectui#8176 made visible`.

## ⚠️ One correction this PR makes to its own first draft — the `data` gate is DOUBLY guarded

The obvious reading of the `data` gate is
`if (schema.objectName && !boundData && !schema.data)`. The first version of the pin asserted that,
and the ablation showed it could **not** be made to fail. Measured cause: `SchemaRenderer` spreads
non-metadata schema properties as React props, so an authored `data` arrives BOTH as `schema.data`
AND as this component's `data` prop; `hasExternalData = Array.isArray(externalData)` is therefore
true and the fetch effect returns at its FIRST line, before that condition is reached.

Three legs, all run: removing `!schema.data` alone — GREEN. Removing `if (hasExternalData) return;`
alone — GREEN. Removing BOTH — both gate rows RED by name. The pin, the registration docblock and
the `MEMBER_PINS` entry now record the mechanism that was measured rather than the one that reads
best. A second, separate defect in the same rows was found the same way: the negatives originally
asserted "no query" immediately after the first card appeared, which is earlier than the query is
ever issued. They now wait through a `settle` window that a CONTROL row proves is long enough by
making a real query observable through exactly that wait.

## Verification

Run through the container's shared verify lock; verdicts read from the runner's own summary lines.

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` | 198 passed (198) |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-kanban/` | 30 files, 204 passed (204) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console test` | 89 files, 1069 passed (1069) |
| `packages/plugin-kanban` `pnpm type-check` | clean |
| `apps/console` `pnpm type-check` | clean |
| `packages/plugin-kanban` `eslint .` | exit 0 — 44 files, 0 errors, 161 warnings |
| `apps/console` `eslint .` | exit 0 — 189 files, 0 errors, 210 warnings |

Both dependency closures were built first (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-kanban^...' build`,
`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build`) — before that build the console type-check reported
TS2307/TS2882 across files this branch never touched, which is the stale-`dist` signature and not a
verdict.

Gates: `check-control-bytes` OK (6621 tracked files) · `check-changeset-presence` OK (4 source files
of 2 released packages, 1 changeset) · `check-changeset-no-major` OK · `check-element-data-source-declaration`
OK · `check-unreferenced-sources` OK · `check-handler-key-read-sites` OK · `check:spec-floors` OK ·
`check-governed-queue-guard --test` on all five changed paths: **NOT GOVERNED** (control: `AGENTS.md`
returns governed, exit 3). `check:sdui-registration-pins` weighs a built console `dist` and is left
to CI; this change touches no `sideEffects` array. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` / `pnpm test` are CI's.

### Parity gate assertion count: 198 → 198, unmoved — and why

Same as slice 1, for the same reason. Every direction in that file is either one aggregate `it()` or
`it.each(covered)` — the population is per-BLOCK, and `object-kanban` was already covered. Four new
keys therefore add rows INSIDE existing per-block assertions rather than adding an `it()`. The count
that did move is the one the keys actually enter: the member-shape population, 84 → 88, all four
answered with pins.

Lint reading is the package-scoped `eslint .` (the CI-equivalent for the packages touched), not a
per-file narrowing: 44 + 189 files linted, 0 errors. ⛔ `--no-inline-config` deliberately not passed
— that is an objectstack convention and manufactures errors this repo's CI does not have. Type-aware
linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js` (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), so this
diff cannot move a verdict on any file it does not touch. Counts read from `--format json`; the
final commit these were taken at is `72778cee`.
